title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: the 'équation des lacets' notes, i.e. the study of GL(2,Ẑ)- and Galois/Teichmüller-type actions on profinite fundamental groups. Here Π is a profinite free group, Π_0 a finite-index subgroup, and S_0^{Π}Γ^! ⊃ S_0^{Π_0}Γ^! are subgroups of a group of triples (u,a,b) cut out by congruence conditions. ε_2 and ε_3 are two sign characters. By the next page they behave like the quadratic characters mod 4 and mod 3 of a determinant-type invariant: u = diag(μ,1) with μ ≡ 1 (4), μ ≡ −1 (3) has ε_2 = 1, ε_3 = −1. For GL(2,Z) itself, ε_2ε_3 = 1.

The group 𝓔 (defined at (79), earlier) is a quotient of order 8. It is a central extension of μ×μ (μ = {±1}) by μ, and the projection to μ×μ is read via (ε_3, ε_2).

The previous page proved the Proposition: x² = 1 in 𝓔 iff ε_3(x) = 1 or ε_2(x)ε_3(x) = 1, i.e. x ∈ 𝓔' ∪ 𝓔''' (91).

This page draws two corollaries.
- Corollary 1: the elements of order 4 are exactly the two lifts of (−1,1), i.e. ε_3 = −1 and ε_2 = 1. They are mutually inverse and generate the unique cyclic subgroup of order 4, which is 𝓔'' = {ε_2 = 1} (92).
- Corollary 2: the extension is non-split. A split central extension is a direct product (μ×μ)×μ, which has exponent 2.

He then views 𝓔 as an extension of 𝓔/𝓔'' ≅ μ by 𝓔'' ≅ Z/4. Since Aut(Z/4) = (Z/4)^* = {±1}, the action of the nontrivial element is ±1, and he sets out to compute the sign. He lifts −1 by the element of (92), x = (τ, τ', τ) ∈ S_0^{Π_0}Γ^{!'''} (cf. (70)). He makes it act on the image of u = (u,a,b) ∈ S_0^{Π}Γ^! with ε_3(u) = −1, ε_2(u) = 1, which is a generator of 𝓔''. The conditions are u ≡ b mod Π̂_0 and u ≡ σa mod Π̂.

On the next page this becomes a congruence (94) with an unknown sign ε. He then notes a difficulty: GL(2,Z) supplies no element with ε_2ε_3 = −1. He therefore passes to GL(2,Ẑ), taking u = diag(μ,1) with μ ≡ 5 (12) and τ = diag(−1,1).

Abstractly, the conclusion is forced by the order count. A non-split central extension of (Z/2)² by Z/2 with exactly two elements of order 4 is the dihedral group D_4 of order 8. Here 𝓔 → 𝓔/𝓔'' splits, because there are involutions outside 𝓔''. So 𝓔 = Z/4 ⋊ Z/2, and a trivial action would give Z/4×Z/2, which has four elements of order 4. Hence the sign is −1 and 𝓔 ≅ D_4.
errors: No mathematical error. The proofs of Corollaries 1 and 2 are correct given the Proposition.

Gap / inefficiency: the sign of the action of 𝓔/𝓔'' on 𝓔'' ≅ Z/4 that he sets out to compute explicitly already follows from Corollary 1. A trivial action would give Z/4×Z/2, which has 4 elements of order 4, not 2. So the action is inversion, 𝓔 ≅ D_4, and the explicit computation in GL(2,Ẑ) begun on the next page is only a consistency check.
Slip in the manuscript/transcription: 'opération ... sur 𝓔'' and 'Aut(𝓔')' should read 𝓔'' (the cyclic subgroup of order 4).

ideas.what: Determining the isomorphism type of an order-8 central extension of (Z/2)^2 by Z/2 via counting involutions and elements of order 4 (characterized by sign characters ε_2, ε_3)
ideas.modern_name: classification of groups of order 8 / extraspecial 2-group D_4 as non-split central extension

ideas.what: Using the quadratic characters mod 3 and mod 4 (of a determinant-type invariant) on GL(2,Ẑ)-type data to detect a finite quotient, and noting that GL(2,Z) only realizes ε_2ε_3 = 1 so that one must pass to GL(2,Ẑ)
ideas.modern_name: congruence characters of GL(2,Ẑ) acting on profinite free groups (level 12 phenomena)
ideas.where_published: related themes in Esquisse d'un programme / La Longue Marche (GL(2,Z) and Teichmüller towers), but not this computation

deep.surprise_reason: Routine finite-group bookkeeping inside a longer computation: identifying a group of order 8 (in fact D_4) via its elements of order 4 and non-splitness. There is no new result or connection on this page.
transcription_corrections: 'opération de 𝓔/𝓔'' = μ sur 𝓔'' — the manuscript writes 𝓔' (or the transcription misreads), but the intended object is 𝓔''; likewise 'Aut(𝓔')' should be Aut(𝓔'') ≃ (Z/4Z)^* ≃ {±1}.
In (93) the congruences read: u ≡ b mod Π̂_0, u ≡ σa mod Π̂.
